cluster_name: Russia-Ukraine drone escalation devastates logistics and oil refineries
tldr: Headlines across 14 country-buckets frame the Russia-Ukraine war as an intensifying two-sided drone campaign targeting economic infrastructure: Russia repeatedly hammering Ukrainian cities and food logistics while Ukraine strikes Russian refineries and e-commerce warehouses. The SECURITY_DEFENSE register dominates — most outlets lead with military-action verbs (hammers, bombards, batters, endures, launches) — while economic consequences appear as secondary headlines from a smaller cluster of outlets. Zelensky’s order to launch 1,000 drones per day surfaces only in exiled Russian press (Meduza), absent from Western and Global South news fronts entirely.
event_summary: Russia struck Ukrainian cities and logistics infrastructure with missiles and drones over multiple days while Ukraine escalated counter-strikes on Russian refineries, ports, and e-commerce warehouses.

outlet_isolation_top.note: Balkan Insight headlines foreground Romania's Black Sea drone interception — a NATO-border security angle absent from all other outlet titles.
Straits Times headline anchors in Ukrainian food logistics destruction, emphasising trade-supply consequences over the bilateral military exchange.
Deutsche Welle leads with grain export disruption and Black Sea port attacks, framing the conflict through global food-supply consequences.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: No Chinese-outlet headlines despite China's stake in Russian oil markets and global grain prices disrupted by Black Sea strikes.
Turkey, which mediates Black Sea grain corridor access and faces direct exposure to maritime drone incidents, is absent from headline coverage.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to headline Zelensky’s order to launch 1,000 drones per day at Russia — a major strategic escalation declaration not foregrounded by any Western or Global South news title.
Only outlet to lead on grain export disruption rather than the military exchange itself, foregrounding global food-supply consequences from the headline’s first word.
Only outlet to headline Kyrgyzstan as a supply-chain casualty of Ukrainian warehouse strikes — a third-country economic spillover invisible in all news headlines.
Only outlet to headline Romania’s military interception of a maritime drone near a Black Sea gas platform, framing NATO-member energy infrastructure as a direct blast-radius target.
Exiled Russian press uniquely headlined Russian oil refining at a 20-year low, quantifying economic damage inside Russia that Western news headlines did not foreground.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents the Russia-Ukraine conflict as a mutual, escalating drone war with the security frame dominant across most outlets; a distinct minority foreground economic consequences (destroyed food storage, stalled grain exports, historic lows in Russian oil refining). The strategic escalation signal — Zelensky ordering 1,000 daily drone launches — surfaces only in exiled Russian press headlines, absent from Western news fronts.
